text: The only thing I wanted to check with Mr Singh was this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because I had understood, when he spoke just now, that there are some things that the Workers' Party or he agrees to.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One is the finding against Ms Raeesah Khan for abuse of privilege.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second thing is that of the fine in respect of the untruths told on 3 August (twice).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That, I think, is not disputed and they agree with that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What they do not agree with is the fine for the third time that she lied, the $10,000, because implicit in that was that she was acting on their guidance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, they do not agree with that and they do not want to vote on that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And then, in respect of the Second Motion, because I had heard him say that he wishes to clear his name and that he will go before and cooperate with the PP, I am asking: is Mr Singh prepared to agree to the part of the Motion which says that he and Mr Faisal Manap be referred to the PP?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I can understand that they do not want to vote on the other parts of the Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, perhaps, if Mr Singh could clarify that part and then we can think about how we can deal with the votes on the two Motions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Implicit in that is an acknowledgement that our actions somehow mitigate the quantum.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Just to be sure that I have this correct.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, for the Second Motion, the Leader of the Opposition and WP will be voting against it in its entirety, is that correct?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But an important caveat is as what I mentioned about Mr Faisal Manap and myself.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We are prepared to be referred to the Public Prosecutor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And for the first one, they would be prepared to vote in favour of the first paragraph, that is, taking note of the special reports.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If you look at the First Motion, the first resolution of the First Motion is to take note of the special reports.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is actually not a resolution, just to take note of the special reports.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you do not have a problem with taking note of the special reports, right?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, paragraph 2, you would have no objection to paragraph 2(a), that is the resolution that resolves that Ms Raeesah Khan is guilty of abuse of privileges of Parliament?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And you have no objection to paragraph 2(b)?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The one that covers the fine of $25,000?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it is really only in respect of the $10,000 fine.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I am just confirming that paragraphs 2(a) and 2(b) you agree with, and paragraph 2(c) you do not agree with.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am not going to ask you anything else, so you may sit down.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Normally, when you vote for a Motion, you vote for the Motion in its entirety.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if there are three things in the Motion and you agree with two, but not one, normally, you would vote against the entire thing, right?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would propose that we do split the Second Motion into two votes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, as moved by the Leader of the House, shall we proceed?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if you will permit, I will then move a Motion now to seek that the Second Motion be allowed to be voted in a split manner as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have now come to the conclusion of the debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I shall put the necessary questions to the House for decision.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will first deal with the Motion on the Committee of Privileges Report (Recommendations in respect of Ms Raeesah Khan).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Agrees with the recommendations of the Committee of Privileges relating to Ms Raeesah Khan, as stated in the Committee’s Report contained in Paper Parl 13 of 2022, and resolves: (proc text)] [(proc text) (a) that Ms Raeesah Khan is guilty of abuse of the privileges of Parliament for an untruth (“Untruth”) spoken in Parliament on 3 August 2021 (twice) and repeated on 4 October 2021; (proc text)]

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Those who are dissenting, please stand in your place so that we can record your dissent.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will now deal with the next question on the Second Motion.
